sermon.title: Are Public Schools Successful?
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In “Are Public Schools Successful?”, Pastor David G. Kincer traces the rise of public education in America, the Protestants’ early reservations, and the beliefs of the groups he says shaped government schools. He says the results have not met the schools’ goals, and he answers with Proverbs 22:6, Proverbs 27:12, Hosea 4:6 and Proverbs 4:7: train children in the way they should go, make them prudent, and make understanding the supreme thing. He calls for change, competition, and home, private and Christian schools as options.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor note: the year he gives for the start of federal grants is garbled in the captions (“18990”) and shown as [unclear]. He says “Proverbs 4” for “wisdom is the principal thing … get understanding,” which is Proverbs 4:7. He dates the Scopes trial to 1926 (it was held in 1925). He names Unitarian, Protestant and Catholic churches, socialists, humanists, the Soviet Union, Nazi Germany, China and Cuba, the teachers unions, the Department of Education and the Democratic Party, all as his own views; these are kept as spoken. His figures (50 million murdered in the Soviet Union, 28th in eighth-grade math and 17th in science, 40% of legislators and teachers using private schools, humanists and liberals as 20% of Americans and 52% of the Democratic Party) and the 1849 Protestant statement he quotes have not been checked here.

chunks.section_question: Are public schools the best choice for our children?
chunks.short_answer: He asks whether public schools are successful and says they are now government schools, where the government, the humanists and the teachers unions decide what is taught. He says early-1800s reformers argued tax-funded schools would create good citizens and prevent crime and poverty.
chunks.text: In this session we will ask the question: are public schools successful? Are they the best choice for our children? Are public schools successful, and are they the best choice in America for our children? Now, in reality the public schools are no longer public schools; they are government schools, as the public have no say anymore. It is the government, the humanist and the teachers unions that decide what academics, what truths and what lies are taught. Now we’re going to look at the rise of public education in the USA. The early 1800s, anti-Christian school reformers, because schools were home schools and Christian schools back then. They strongly favored, you, by Unitarian and liberal churches and socialists, and they argued that public schools funded by property tax would create good citizens, prevent crime, unite society around secularism, of course, and prevent poverty. That’s in the early 1800s.

chunks.section_question: What did Protestants first think about public schools?
chunks.short_answer: He says Protestants had reservations and decided to give public schools a test; in 1849 they favored them, saying the Bible deficiencies could be supplied outside the school.
chunks.text: Now, the Protestants at that time, they had some reservation, they had some cautions about public school systems supported by taxes, and so they were going to give it a test. And, uh, in 1849 they favored it, but they said this: “The benefits of the system are so many, and the benefits are so great for a public school, that its religious or Bible deficiencies, that can be supplied outside the public school, are not a sufficient reason for abandoning it.”

chunks.section_question: Is Sunday school enough to balance public school?
chunks.short_answer: He says Protestants promised parochial schools if the experiment failed, but children get a lopsided portion: 40 hours a week of public school with secular teachers and texts against about 3 hours a week of church.
chunks.text: They go on to say, “If, after a full and faithful experiment, that it is proven that loyalty to the religious interest or Bible interest of our children forbids the support of public education, we will establish parochial schools in which full doctrinal, religious, Bible instruction is possible.” But the problem here is, we’re given a lopsided portion: 40 hours a week to public school, with 3 hours a week to church, Sunday school and teaching. And the secular teachers and the secular text, versus Christian teachers with Christian text, Bible text, has a lopsided impact, and that’s something that the Protestants overlooked.

chunks.section_question: How did public education rise in America?
chunks.short_answer: He lists points such as support from Unitarian and liberal churches and socialists, property-tax funding, Catholics keeping their parochial schools, the McGuffey Readers, the National Teachers Association in 1857 and the federal Department of Education in 1867.
chunks.text: Now we’re going to give you eight points in the rise of public education. Two, we’ve already hit: Unitarian, liberal churches and socialists greatly favor it, that ought to ring your bell; funded by property tax, now I can lose my property if I don’t pay my taxes. Number three, the Protestants has reservations until 1960 that they never followed up on. Number four, the Catholics kept their parochial schools, their local church schools, and rejected totally the public schools. The King James Bible and McGuffey Readers were the prominent readers in the early public schools, so the Protestants got fooled and thought they had no problem. But in 1857, point number five, National Teachers Association, now we got a union. 1867, the federal Department of Education, now we got the feds involved, and they started giving money grants in [unclear].

chunks.section_question: What beliefs shaped the early public school movement?
chunks.short_answer: He says compulsory attendance laws came by 1918 and education became a civil monopoly. He says liberal Unitarians and socialists persuaded people that the Bible has errors and that all religions lead to the same God, and wanted a socialist government.
chunks.text: By 1918 every state had a compulsory attendance law. And number eight, this wound up being a civil monopoly on education with no competition. We’re going to give you four inviting persuasions during the public schools’ rise, people trying to persuade you to go their way. First, the liberal Unitarian Christians and the socialists in the early 1800s. They persuaded people that the Bible is not literal, it’s not truth, it’s got errors in it; you got to re- use reason, not the Bible; all religions lead to the same God; there’s no virgin birth, no second coming, Jesus isn’t God, no sin atonement, no resurrection, no miracles, no- evolution is the way they say creation happened; government gives aid to the poor, the sick, the social ills, and public education. They want a socialist government, and they had no opposition from cons- from conservatives from 1926 to 1960.

chunks.section_question: What did Bible fundamentalists believe, and why did they leave politics?
chunks.short_answer: He says they held that the Bible is truth, Jesus is God, born of a virgin, died for sin, rose and is coming again, but they dropped out of politics after the Scopes trial. He compares the Communist Manifesto and an American socialist manifesto, both calling for government-run schools.
chunks.text: In the early 1800s, the Bible fundamentalists had the opposite beliefs, and they wrote a book about it in 1915: the Bible is a book of truth, it doesn’t have errors in it; that Jesus is God; he was born of a virgin; the Trinity; Jesus died for sin and rose again; he’s coming back again; there’s an eternal judgment; there are supernatural miracles; there’s a six-day creation; and people are supposed to help them- themselves and help others, not government. They support capitalism, and they dropped out of politics after the Scopes trial of 1926, leaving the humanists, the socialists and the liberals unopposed until the 1960s. In 1848 the Communist Manifesto was written. The American Socialist Manifesto was written in 1919; it was exactly the same, they just changed the name to socialist. Property, banks, transportation, media, factories and farms all belong to the government; a heavy income tax supported it; equal pay for everyone; no inheritance; redistribution of the population; they abolished all religions; and they established free education for all children, and the government ran schools. Asia went communist, Europe went socialist, and they’re trying to get America.

chunks.section_question: What is secular humanism, according to the sermon?
chunks.short_answer: He says secular humanism arose in 1933 believing in evolution, no supernatural God, no prayer, and reason instead of the Bible, promoted through the schools. He points to Soviet government schools as a result.
chunks.text: The religion of secular humanism arised in 1933. They believed, like the liberals and the Unitarian church: evolution, no creation, no life after death, the scientific method is all we need, no supernatural God, no prayer, no worship, we need reason and intellect, not the Bible, and we’re going to promote our beliefs about through the educational system; churches and their rituals and their methods, their activities, must be altered and changed; capitalism is inadequate; socialized, equal distribution economy is what the humanists promoted. So what was the results of humanism in public schools? Well, in the Soviet Union, 1917, compulsory attendance, tax-supported government schools taught students to be loyal to a government that sent millions to slave labor camps in Siberia, starved to death peasants in the Ukraine, closed all churches, persecuted Christians, seized all property, and murdered 50 million opponents simply because they opposed them.

chunks.section_question: What happened when governments controlled the schools?
chunks.short_answer: He says in Nazi Germany compulsory public schools turned children into “genocidal monsters,” and that American public schools have produced more addiction, teen sex, dropouts, illiteracy and school violence.
chunks.text: The schools provided the willing hands, and the police and the army provided the fear. The National Socialists ruled Germany from 1933 to 1945, using its compulsory attendance, tax-supported public schools to turn ordinary German children into genocidal monsters. German soldiers and the secret police committed horrible atrocities against any citizens that opposed the government. And time forbids the facts on China, Cuba and other dictator humanist nations committing atrocities on mankind. In the United States of America, in the public schools, has produce more alcoholics, more addicts, drug addicts, more smokers, more teen sex, more, more sexually transmitted diseases and more immorality; produced more dropouts from high school, functional illiterates, and more school violence. Not a very good result in the American public schools.

chunks.section_question: Does more money improve public schools?
chunks.short_answer: He says more tax money and even lotteries brought lower results, with America 28th in eighth-grade math and 17th in science. He says most students lack drive and duty, and government schools have not achieved their goals.
chunks.text: They took more tax money to try to improve education, even the lotteries, the government got in the gambling business to help support education, with lower results. More money, lower results. The international scoring: we are 28th in eighth-grade math and 17th in eighth-grade science in the industrialized global nations. Most students lack drive, they lack effort, they lack duty and responsibility to get educated and learn a job skill. Entertainment seems to be their main focus. In America, government schools thus has not achieved its goals, but they have promoted socialism, humanism and immorality, not only in our public schools but in society.

chunks.section_question: What does “train up a child in the way he should go” mean for schools?
chunks.short_answer: From Proverbs 22:6 he lists what children should not be taught, and from Proverbs 27:12 and Hosea 4:6 he says schools should produce prudent students with the knowledge to make good decisions.
chunks.text: Well, the solutions to education, for your consideration. Proverbs 22:6: train up a child in the way he should go. A child shouldn’t be taught to become a homosexual, a thief, an adulterer, liar, a sluggard, a lazy person that doesn’t work, ignorant, can’t read, can’t write, can’t communicate, can’t calculate, and they shouldn’t be taught to be a criminal. Teen sex and all of its sexually transmitted diseases shouldn’t be taught. They shouldn’t be taught to use alcohol, drugs, tobacco, which is killing thousands of Americans every year and physically harming millions of Americans every year. Profanity and witchcraft and such like should not be taught. We should be training them up in the way they should go. Proverbs 27:12: a prudent person foresees the evil, the danger, the harm, and hides himself, but the simple, the open-minded, they go on and are punished. And the school system should be producing prudent students that have avoids the dangers. My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge, Hosea 4:6. A school system should give children knowledge to make good decisions, so that they don’t do things that will damage them financially, physically, or even bring death upon them.

chunks.section_question: How important is education in the Bible?
chunks.short_answer: Quoting Proverbs 4, he says wisdom is the supreme thing, and God says educating our children and ourselves is the top priority; we can’t cut cost or time.
chunks.text: In Proverbs also, it’s at Proverbs 4, it says wisdom is the supreme thing, and in all your getting, get wisdom, and get understanding; if it cost you all you have, get understanding. And so God says that educating our children and ourselves is the top priority, and we got to put every amount of time is needed and every amount of money that’s needed. We can’t cut cost and we can’t cut time to educate our children to be prudent young people. Now, with these facts that I’ve presented to you, public schools are not the best choices.

chunks.section_question: What are the alternatives to public schools?
chunks.short_answer: He calls for a competitive system where the best school wins the tax money and the parents’ approval, and until then names home schools, private schools and Christian schools as options. He faults Protestants, humanists, liberals and the Democratic Party.
chunks.text: Consider this: 40% of legislators and 40% of public school teachers put their kids in private schools. Legislators and public school teachers should, because they’re involved, to know what’s going on, rise up and fight for a change in the public school system. We need to ax the failed unions and the Department of Education; they haven’t done their job. We need to form and start a competitive system where the best school wins the tax money and the approval of the parent. Until then, the home schools, the private schools and Christian schools are a possible alternative, a possible option, for those who want their kids trained up in the way they should go. We can fault Protestants for supporting bad government schools all these years and for quitting on public issues. We can fault the humanists and the liberals, who are 20% of the population of America; they are 52% of the Democratic Party. So we can fault the Democratic Party, the humanists and liberals, because they’re the ones promoting this kind of education in the American schools.
